backlog.title: BUG-001 Fix: Restore auto Commit-Style Feature (maxEntries → maxCount)
backlog.description: Fix the critical defect where getRecentCommitMessages() passes an invalid simple-git option ({ maxEntries } instead of { maxCount }), which causes the DEFAULT 'auto' commit-style to throw on every commit and silently degrade to the placeholder message. This single-character-class bug makes the headline feature of session 012 (PRD §5.1 Commit Message Style) 100% non-functional under default configuration. The fix spans the root-cause code change, the masked test assertion correction, and regression-prevention integration tests that use real simple-git instead of mocks.

milestones.title: Fix Root Cause and Prevent Regression
milestones.description: Correct the invalid simple-git option name in getRecentCommitMessages(), fix the test assertion that validated the wrong contract, and add integration tests that exercise real simple-git so an invalid option name can never be masked by mocks again.

tasks.title: Fix the invalid simple-git option and its masked test assertion
tasks.description: Change { maxEntries: count } to { maxCount: count } in getRecentCommitMessages() at src/tools/git-mcp.ts:590, and correct the corresponding test assertion at tests/unit/tools/git-mcp.test.ts:977 from { maxEntries: 2 } to { maxCount: 2 }. These two changes are an atomic pair: the test currently validates the broken contract, so both must be updated together.

subtasks.title: Fix getRecentCommitMessages to use maxCount instead of maxEntries
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Confirmed in plan/012_7dd502f7feb9/bugfix/001_662720d16c77/architecture/system_context.md — the simple-git LogOptions interface (node_modules/simple-git/dist/src/lib/tasks/log.d.ts) defines `maxCount?: number`, NOT `maxEntries`. Empirically verified: `git.log({ maxEntries: 3 })` throws `fatal: ambiguous argument 'maxEntries=3'`, while `git.log({ maxCount: 3 })` returns 3 commits correctly. Under the DEFAULT config (PRP_COMMIT_STYLE=auto, PRP_COMMIT_STYLE_EXAMPLES=5), this throw propagates through generateCommitMessage → smartCommit retry → fallback placeholder, making the entire 'auto' commit-style feature non-functional.
2. INPUT: The existing function getRecentCommitMessages(count, repoPath?) at src/tools/git-mcp.ts:583-593 receives a numeric `count` (the PRP_COMMIT_STYLE_EXAMPLES value, default 5) and an optional repoPath.
3. LOGIC: Change ONLY the option key at line 590 from `{ maxEntries: count }` to `{ maxCount: count }`. This is a one-token change. Do NOT change any other logic — the function signature, the count===0 short-circuit, the validateRepositoryPath call, the return mapping (logResult.all.map(entry => entry.message)), or the JSDoc. The fix aligns the code with the simple-git LogOptions contract. Per the project AGENTS.md Rule 5, this is an out-of-spec corrective fix (bug in existing behavior) — a PRD bugfix-section entry is welcome but not blocking.
4. OUTPUT: getRecentCommitMessages now correctly calls git.log({ maxCount: count }) and returns string[] of recent commit messages without throwing. This output is consumed by generateCommitMessage() at src/utils/git-commit.ts:358-360 for the 'auto' style-resolution path. After this fix, the 'auto' style will function correctly under default config.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. The getRecentCommitMessages JSDoc (lines 570-582) accurately describes the function's behavior and does not mention the internal option name; no update needed. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Fix the masked test assertion in git-mcp.test.ts from maxEntries to maxCount
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Confirmed in plan/012_7dd502f7feb9/bugfix/001_662720d16c77/architecture/system_context.md — the unit test at tests/unit/tools/git-mcp.test.ts:977 asserts `expect(mockGitInstance.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ maxEntries: 2 })`, which validates the BROKEN contract. The mockGitInstance.log is a bare vi.fn() that ignores its arguments, so the assertion passes while validating the wrong option name. This is the primary reason CI is green despite the critical bug. The test's inline comment at line 975 also says 'log called with maxEntries' — update that comment too.
2. INPUT: The fix from P1.M1.T1.S1 has changed the production code to use { maxCount: count }. The test must now assert the correct contract.
3. LOGIC: At tests/unit/tools/git-mcp.test.ts, change line 977 from `expect(mockGitInstance.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ maxEntries: 2 })` to `expect(mockGitInstance.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ maxCount: 2 })`. Also update the comment at line 975 from 'log called with maxEntries' to 'log called with maxCount'. Do NOT change the mockGitInstance.log setup or any other part of the test — the mock setup (mockResolvedValue with canned commit data) remains valid. The only change is the assertion's expected option name. Run `npx vitest run tests/unit/tools/git-mcp.test.ts` to confirm the test passes.
4. OUTPUT: The unit test now asserts the correct simple-git contract ({ maxCount: 2 }), so it would fail if the bug is reintroduced. This test serves as a first-line defense; P1.M1.T2 adds deeper integration tests.
5. DOCS: none — test-only change with no user-facing surface. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Add regression-prevention integration tests using real simple-git
tasks.description: Add integration tests that call REAL simple-git (not vi.fn mocks) against throwaway temp git repos, so an invalid option name fails the build instead of being masked. Two test layers: (1) a direct integration test for getRecentCommitMessages that creates a real temp git repo with seeded commits, and (2) an end-to-end test that drives generateCommitMessage under the default 'auto' config (with only the LLM agent mocked) and asserts it does not throw on a repo with >1 commit.

subtasks.title: Integration test for getRecentCommitMessages using real simple-git against a temp git repo
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Confirmed in plan/012_7dd502f7feb9/bugfix/001_662720d16c77/architecture/external_deps.md — no existing 'createTestRepo' helper exists. Temp-repo pattern is inlined in tests/unit/config/hack-config.test.ts using mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'prefix-')) + rmSync(dir, {recursive:true, force:true}) in afterEach. Integration tests live in tests/integration/. The existing tests/integration/smart-commit.test.ts mocks git-commit.ts itself, so it does NOT test real git operations — a gap this test fills. simple-git ^3.30.0 is installed.
2. INPUT: The fixed getRecentCommitMessages() from P1.M1.T1.S1 now uses git.log({ maxCount: count }). This test validates that fix against real git.
3. LOGIC: Create a new integration test file (e.g., tests/integration/git-mcp-log.test.ts) that: (a) Creates a temp directory via mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'git-log-test-')). (b) Initializes a real git repo: use simpleGit(dir).init() then addConfig('user.email','test@test.com') and addConfig('user.name','Test'). (c) Seeds N commits (N > 1, e.g., 5) by writing files and calling simpleGit(dir).add('.') + simpleGit(dir).commit('message N'). Use distinct messages like 'feat: commit 1', 'fix: commit 2', etc. (d) Calls the REAL getRecentCommitMessages(count, dir) (imported from src/tools/git-mcp.ts — do NOT mock it or simple-git). (e) Asserts it returns the expected messages in newest-first order without throwing. (f) Test with count < total (e.g., 3 of 5), count === total (5 of 5), and count === 0 (short-circuit, returns []). (g) Clean up with rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }) in afterEach. CRITICAL: Do NOT mock simple-git or getRecentCommitMessages — the whole point is to catch invalid option names. Import getRecentCommitMessages from '../../src/tools/git-mcp.js'. The validateRepositoryPath call inside getRecentCommitMessages needs a valid git repo at the given path, so the temp dir must be git-init'd. NOTE: validateRepositoryPath may require the path to be inside the project — check its implementation; if it rejects external tmpdir paths, use the project's tests/tmp/ directory or adjust accordingly (mock validateRepositoryPath to passthrough only if strictly necessary, but do NOT mock simpleGit or git.log).
4. OUTPUT: An integration test that fails immediately if getRecentCommitMessages uses any invalid simple-git option. This test directly validates PRD Recommendation #2 (add integration test with real simple-git). The test file lives at tests/integration/git-mcp-log.test.ts (or similar) and is picked up by the default vitest config (include: ['tests/**/*.{test,spec}.ts']).
5. DOCS: none — test-only addition with no user-facing surface. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: End-to-end test for generateCommitMessage under default auto config (LLM agent mocked only)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Confirmed in plan/012_7dd502f7feb9/bugfix/001_662720d16c77/architecture/system_context.md — the existing git-commit.test.ts style-resolution tests (line 1085+) mock BOTH getRecentCommitMessages (vi.fn() at line 28) and createCommitMessageAgent (vi.fn()), so the 'auto' path never exercises real git. This masked the maxEntries bug entirely. The fix from P1.M1.T1.S1 changes the option to maxCount, but without a test that uses REAL getRecentCommitMessages against a real repo, the same masking could recur. The generateCommitMessage function (src/utils/git-commit.ts:344-375) calls getRecentCommitMessages(n) when style==='auto' && n>0, then calls createCommitMessageAgent(system) → agent.prompt(prompt) for the LLM call.
2. INPUT: The fixed getRecentCommitMessages from P1.M1.T1.S1 (now uses maxCount). The generateCommitMessage function from src/utils/git-commit.ts. The config getters getPrpCommitStyle() (returns 'auto' by default) and getPrpCommitStyleExamples() (returns 5 by default).
3. LOGIC: Add an integration test (in the same or a new test file under tests/integration/) that: (a) Creates a temp git repo with >1 commit (same pattern as P1.M1.T2.S1 — mkdtempSync, simpleGit(dir).init(), seed 3+ commits). (b) Mocks ONLY the LLM boundary — mock src/agents/commit-message-agent.js's createCommitMessageAgent to return a fake agent whose .prompt() resolves to { status: 'success', data: 'feat: generated commit message', error: null }. Do NOT mock getRecentCommitMessages or simple-git. (c) Sets process.env such that getPrpCommitStyle() returns 'auto' and getPrpCommitStyleExamples() returns 5 (env unset = defaults, or explicitly stub). (d) Calls generateCommitMessage('some diff text'). CRITICAL: generateCommitMessage calls getRecentCommitMessages(n) with no repoPath arg (it uses the current working directory). To make this work against the temp repo, either: (i) spy on process.cwd() to return the temp dir (existing pattern in git-commit.test.ts:132: vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue('/project')), or (ii) if getRecentCommitMessages is called without repoPath and validateRepositoryPath uses process.cwd(), ensure the temp repo is at the cwd mock target. (e) Asserts generateCommitMessage does NOT throw and returns a non-empty descriptive message (NOT the fallback placeholder). (f) Cleans up env and temp dir in afterEach. NOTE: The test must verify the DEFAULT config path specifically — this is the path the bug broke. If mocking cwd, ensure validateRepositoryPath accepts it (it may check for .git existence — the temp repo has .git after init()).
4. OUTPUT: An end-to-end test that validates the full 'auto' style path (config resolution → real getRecentCommitMessages → real git.log → agent factory wiring → message return) under default config against a real repo with >1 commit. This test directly validates PRD Recommendation #3 (add e2e test for default auto config). It would have caught BUG-001 before it shipped.
5. DOCS: none — test-only addition with no user-facing surface. This rides WITH the work.
